content.stringValue:
Our new case starts at Cavite on 20 January 1872. A mutiny is a military uprising against authority. The NHCP execution-site marker links the later accusation against three priests with this January event.

Keep two places separate: Cavite is linked with the uprising; Bagumbayan in Manila is linked with the later execution. Related events in the same year are not necessarily the same event. This introductory timeline does not settle every disagreement about the causes or extent of the uprising.

Your museum task is to locate the event accurately. We study what happened without acting as fighters.

content.stringValue:
After the uprising, colonial authorities accused the priests of involvement. The NHCP marker describes their involvement as alleged. Alleged means claimed, rather than proven merely by saying it. The National Museum describes suspected treason: a charge of acting against the government to which a person owes allegiance.

A caption should distinguish the accusation from proof. A serious punishment does not by itself prove that an accusation was true. Our classroom cards cannot replace examination of historical records.

Repair this fictional label: "They were accused, so they must have organized the mutiny." An accusation and a proven action are different. You are not asked to decide guilt from three short clues.

content.stringValue:
Your case has three parts. Locate the Cavite Mutiny on 20 January 1872. Explain that authorities accused Gomes, Burgos and Zamora, and that the priests were executed at Bagumbayan on 17 February. Then identify later remembrance, such as Rizal's dedication.

The sequence connects events without confusing them. Punishment does not turn an accusation into proof. Later remembrance helps explain why the case remained important in concerns about justice and the country.

Complete this report frame silently or with a trusted adult: "The event was ___. The accusation was ___. A later response was ___. It shows ___, but does not prove ___." The quiz checks five lesson topics. If one is difficult, review its scene before targeted practice.

title.stringValue: Cavite and GOMBURZA: Events, Claims and Remembrance

lessonRecap.stringValue: The Cavite Mutiny was a military uprising on 20 January 1872; the later execution was a separate event. GOMBURZA remembers the three priests; reform advocacy alone does not prove involvement in the mutiny. Distinguish the authorities' accusation from evidence of an action; accusation or punishment alone does not prove involvement. The 20 January mutiny preceded the 17 February execution at Bagumbayan in 1872. Rizal's dedication records remembrance and concern about injustice; it does not prove eyewitness knowledge or a single nationwide response.
